summary: Atlus's character-driven Megami Tensei spinoff series, covering the main RPGs, enhanced editions, fighting/rhythm/dungeon-crawler spinoffs, action and tactics sequels, mobile entries, and announced remakes.

entries.title: Revelations: Persona
entries.definitive_edition: Shin Megami Tensei: Persona PSP release

emulation.notes: Use increased internal resolution and texture filtering to improve the PSP image.

primary.version: Shin Megami Tensei: Persona PSP release
primary.why: The PSP remake is the later official release of the first Persona and is the most complete practical route compared with the original PlayStation and Japan-only Windows versions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version on hardware or PPSSPP with increased internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original localization and soundtrack differences are historical caveats; this entry recommends the PSP route for a modern full play.

entries.title: Persona 2: Innocent Sin

emulation.notes: Use PSP emulation with increased internal resolution.

primary.why: The PSP version added features and a new scenario and is the official worldwide route for Innocent Sin.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version on hardware or PPSSPP with increased internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern PC/console port identified.

entries.title: Persona 2: Eternal Punishment

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for the complete PSP route; use DuckStation for the English PlayStation route.

primary.why: The PSP remake added a new scenario by the original writer, making it the most complete version even though it remained Japan-only.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version on hardware or PPSSPP if language access is solved; otherwise use the PSN/PlayStation original for official English.

secondary.exclusive_content: Official English localization of Eternal Punishment.
secondary.what_to_play: Use the PlayStation/PSN release if English text is required.
secondary.why: The PSP remake did not reach the West, while the original PlayStation version was re-released worldwide on PSN.

entries.remaster_caveats: PSP version's lack of official Western release is the main caveat.

entries.title: Persona 3

emulation.notes: Use native Windows for Reload; use PCSX2 or PPSSPP only for legacy comparison or Portable's original PSP release.

primary.why: Reload is the modern Unreal Engine remake, and the Expansion Pass adds Episode Aigis -The Answer-; Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 3 Reload on Windows with the Expansion Pass installed, including Episode Aigis -The Answer-.

secondary.what_to_play: Play Persona 3 Portable's female-protagonist path after the Reload main route if that route matters.
secondary.why: Portable adds a female playable character route that is not part of Reload.

entries.remaster_caveats: Portable's female protagonist route remains a separate content path; FES is now mainly a legacy comparison route.

entries.title: Persona 3 FES

primary.why: FES is the PS2 director's cut with added content and an epilogue; PCSX2 gives it the highest-fidelity legacy route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 3 FES with PCSX2 at increased internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: For the overall Persona 3 story route, Reload plus Expansion Pass is the modern recommendation; this row preserves the FES edition.

entries.title: Persona 3 Portable

primary.why: The 2023 PC release is the highest-fidelity official route for Portable and preserves its female protagonist path.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 3 Portable on Windows/Steam or Microsoft Store.

entries.remaster_caveats: Portable is not a replacement for Reload's presentation; keep it for the female protagonist route.

entries.title: Persona 3 Reload

primary.why: Windows gives the highest-fidelity route for Reload, and the Expansion Pass includes Episode Aigis -The Answer- as extended story content.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 3 Reload on Windows with the Expansion Pass installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: Female protagonist content from Portable is still outside Reload and should be handled as a separate Portable route.

entries.title: Persona 4

primary.why: Persona 4 Golden is the expanded version with added features/content, and the modern Windows release is the highest-fidelity current route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 4 Golden on Windows/Steam or Microsoft Store.

entries.remaster_caveats: Persona 4 Revival is a future remake and should be reassessed after launch.

entries.title: Persona 4 Golden

primary.why: The modern PC release carries Golden's added content to the highest-fidelity official platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 4 Golden on Windows/Steam or Microsoft Store.

entries.remaster_caveats: Persona 4 Revival is a future remake and not yet part of this recommendation.

entries.title: Persona 5

primary.why: Royal is the enhanced version of Persona 5, and the 2022 Windows port is the highest-fidelity content-complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 5 Royal on Windows/Steam or Microsoft Store.

entries.remaster_caveats: The original Persona 5 remains historically relevant but is not the recommended full route.

entries.title: Persona 4 Arena

emulation.notes: Use console hardware or compatible emulation where lawful.

primary.why: The first Arena has no separate modern PC port identified; the original HD console release is the core route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 4 Arena on PS3/Xbox 360 hardware or compatible preservation setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Persona 4 Arena Ultimax's remaster is a separate sequel/revision entry, not a replacement row here.

entries.title: Persona 4 Arena Ultimax

primary.why: The 2022 remaster brought Ultimax to Steam, Switch, and PS4; Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 4 Arena Ultimax on Windows/Steam.

entries.remaster_caveats: No separate exclusive-content platform identified.

entries.title: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth

emulation.notes: Use increased internal resolution and a readable dual-screen layout.

entries.title: Persona 5 Royal

emulation.notes: Use a controller for the intended JRPG interface, cap frame rate if any animation/timing oddities appear, and avoid the PS4 version unless preserving the original Royal launch context.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Highest via PC resolution and frame-rate settings; 2022 ports are the content-complete baseline.

primary.why: No Sami platform was specified. Windows is the best main route because it uses the 2022 Royal port with the paid Royal DLC included, while PC also has the highest configurable fidelity ceiling through resolution, frame-rate, and display settings compared with fixed console targets.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam or Microsoft Store Windows version with the latest patch, target native/high-resolution output and a stable 60-120 fps cap, and claim the included DLC from the in-game cardboard box once it becomes available.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PS4 Royal release does not have the same included paid-DLC packaging as the 2022 ports. The PS5 version has no PS4 upgrade path or save-data transfer.

entries.title: Persona 5 Strikers

primary.why: Strikers shipped on PS4, Switch, and Windows; the PC release supports Full HD and up to 4K, making it the fidelity pick.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 5 Strikers on Windows/Steam.

entries.remaster_caveats: No enhanced edition identified.

entries.title: Persona 5 Tactica
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release plus Repaint Your Heart DLC

primary.version: PC release plus Repaint Your Heart DLC
primary.why: Tactica shipped on PC and modern consoles, and its Repaint Your Heart DLC adds extra characters and battles; Windows is the highest-fidelity complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 5 Tactica on Windows/Steam with the Repaint Your Heart Challenge Pack if complete content is desired.

entries.remaster_caveats: No enhanced edition identified.

entries.title: Persona 5: The Phantom X

emulation.notes: Use official Windows or mobile clients.

primary.why: The Phantom X launched worldwide for Android, iOS, and Windows; Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the service game.
primary.how_to_play: Play Persona 5: The Phantom X on Windows via the official PC client where the service is available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service availability and regional account handling are the main caveats.

primary.how_to_play: Do not assign a play route until final PC/console builds and content are verified after release.
